subject.title: Bug: sandbox.mode: "non-main" silently breaks sessions_spawn subagent initialization

question: Should sandboxed `sessions_spawn` keep returning `accepted` and surface Docker startup failures asynchronously, or preflight enough sandbox startup work to reject before returning?
rationale: The choice affects the public non-blocking spawn contract, session registry semantics, timeout behavior, and overlap with the broader lifecycle-event work, so automation should not choose it alone.

options.title: Terminalize async startup failures
options.body: Keep the accepted response contract and make Docker startup failure visible as typed terminal state in logs, session history, subagent status, and waits.

options.title: Preflight sandbox before accept
options.body: Move enough sandbox initialization before the accepted response to fail fast, accepting added latency and compatibility review for existing callers.

options.title: Fold into lifecycle tracker
options.body: Close or defer the sandbox-specific path only after https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/58776 has a current-main fix that proves this Docker startup case too.

recommendation.title: Terminalize async startup failures
recommendation.body: Keep the accepted response contract and make Docker startup failure visible as typed terminal state in logs, session history, subagent status, and waits.

likelyOwner.reason: The recent subagent handoff and orchestration history makes this the best available owner for the spawn/sandbox lifecycle contract choice.
